slides.title: Starter Activity: 6-Question Retrieval Grid (Power, Current, Plug Pins & Transformers)

reveals.question: 1. State the equation linking power (P), current (I), and potential difference (V). Calculate the power of a toaster running at 230 V that draws a current of 4 A.
reveals.expectedAnswer: P = I × V = 4 A × 230 V = 920 W (requires a 5 A or 13 A fuse).

reveals.question: 2. State the equation linking power (P), current (I), and resistance (R). By what factor does heating power increase if the current flowing through a resistor triples?
reveals.expectedAnswer: P = I² × R. Power is proportional to current squared (I²), so tripling current increases power by 9× (3² = 9).

reveals.question: 3. Define electric current and state the equation linking charge (Q), current (I), and time (t). How does the direction of electron flow compare to conventional current?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge (Q = I × t). Electrons flow from negative to positive; conventional current flows positive to negative.

reveals.question: 4. Identify the 3 pins in a UK plug (Live, Neutral, Earth) by their positions and wire colours. Which pin connects directly to the fuse, and why?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Live = Brown (bottom right, connects to fuse); Neutral = Blue (bottom left); Earth = Green/Yellow (top center). Fuse isolates live 230 V supply.

reveals.question: 5. Why is the earth pin made longer than the live and neutral pins, and why are all plug pins manufactured from solid brass?
reveals.expectedAnswer: Longer earth pin opens socket safety shutters and connects earth first for protection. Brass is a rigid, corrosion-resistant, high conductor.

reveals.question: 6. Explain why step-up and step-down transformers are used in the National Grid transmission system.
reveals.expectedAnswer: Step-up transformers increase voltage (up to 400 kV) to reduce current, drastically cutting thermal energy losses (P = I²R) in cables. Step-down reduces to 230 V for safety.
